headline_for_review: ANOM-5 IS THE ESTIMATOR -- SPECIFICALLY ITS NULL OBJECT, NOT ITS ARITHMETIC. D_T in the mid band is a sum over only nb_iteration INDEPENDENT ITERATIONS, and per-iteration occupancy reaches 0.739 there. For a non-negative integer X, X^2 >= X gives Var(X) >= E[X] - E[X]^2, so under ANY independent-iteration model E[phi] >= mean_T(1 - mu_T/N) = 0.91826 for the n=43 mid band -- NOT 1. BATCH-014 measured against the Poisson point 1.0, which sits in the INTERIOR of the admissible set. The Coordinator re-derived the inequality and confirmed the deep-tail floors 0.99974/0.99986 are consistent with the same formula at occupancy 0.0023/0.0011. Consequence: z goes -2.45 to -1.43 against the tightest admissible null, and most of ANOM-5 dissolves.
consequences_that_cut_both_ways: THE DEEP-TAIL NULL IS UNAFFECTED AND THEREFORE STANDS. Occupancy there is 0.0023 and 0.0011, so the floor is 0.9997 and 0.9999 and the Poisson point null was the right one. BATCH-014's T-1 survives this batch intact; what it loses is the ANOM-5 bound that EV-MLKEM-c50030 attached to it.

A NEW OPEN ITEM IS CREATED, in the opposite direction. The same correction makes n=50's mid band MORE over-dispersed, +1.66 sd to +2.25 sd. The producer recorded this symmetric consequence rather than reporting only the favourable half.

BATCH-012's DEEP-TAIL TABLE IS NOW CHECKABLE AND THE FLAGS WERE RIGHT. With residuals archived, n=43 M1a's deep-tail ratio reads 0.7974 under a whole-band fit against 2.3938 under a C>=1000 fit. So 'the deep tail sits below its floor' is a property of the whole-band-fitted NORMALISATION for M1/M1a/M3, not a fit-independent fact. That materially qualifies a claim this goal has carried since BATCH-012.
a_second_congenial_control_found_degener: BATCH-014's control_observed_count_binning is DEGENERATE in the n=43 mid band: it closes on the OBSERVED count crossing 10, every mid-band increment is at least 6, so it yields 297 bins against 301 and its congenial 0.8008 reading tests almost nothing. This is the second control in two batches whose agreeable number did not survive reading its code. The real exclusion of binning is that the expected-count binner gives 301 bins over 301 scores, leaving no binning freedom at all.
